record.paper_title: Some open problems in mathematical relativity
record.original_question: Can one prove that the only solution of the vacuum Robinson-Trautman equations on S2 x R with positive mass is the Schwarzschild metric, and can an analogous theorem be proved for the Einstein-Maxwell Robinson-Trautman equations?

evidence.quote: Show that the only solution of the vacuum Robinson-Trautman equations on S2xR with mass > 0, is the Schwarzschild metric [RA;SB2;LPPS]. Can a similar theorem for the Einstein-Maxwell RT equations be shown?

artifact.self_contained_problem:
A vacuum Robinson–Trautman spacetime is a four-dimensional Lorentzian manifold whose metric, in Robinson–Trautman coordinates $(u,r,x^A)$ with $A=2,3$, has the form
$$g = -\Big(K - 2r\,\partial_u \log P - \frac{2m(u)}{r}\Big)\,du^2 - 2\,du\,dr + \frac{2r^2}{P(u,x)^2}\, h_{AB}(x)\,dx^A dx^B,$$
where $h_{AB}$ is the round metric on $S^2$, $P=P(u,x)$ is a positive smooth function on $\mathbb{R}\times S^2$, $K = K(u,x)$ is the Gauss curvature of the conformally rescaled two-metric $P^{-2}h$, and $m(u)>0$ is a positive mass function. The vacuum Einstein equations reduce to the Robinson–Trautman equation
$$12\, m\, \partial_u \log P = \Delta_{P^{-2}h} K,$$
together with $\partial_u m = -\frac{1}{12 m}\, \overline{|\nabla K|^2}$ (or equivalently a parabolic flow for $P$ on $S^2$).

Problem 1. Suppose the underlying manifold has topology $S^2 \times \mathbb{R}$ (with $r>0$) and the total mass parameter is strictly positive. Show that the only complete solution of the vacuum Robinson–Trautman equations on this manifold is the Schwarzschild metric (for which $P$ is the standard stereographic conformal factor and $m$ is constant).

Problem 2. Formulate and prove the analogous statement for the Einstein–Maxwell Robinson–Trautman system, i.e. show that, with positive mass and appropriate (e.g. non-trivial) Maxwell field, the only solution on $S^2\times\mathbb{R}$ is the Reissner–Nordström metric.
artifact.status_search_result: Chruściel (1991, CMP 137) and subsequent work established semi-global existence and convergence of vacuum Robinson–Trautman solutions on $S^2\times\mathbb{R}$ to the Schwarzschild metric for smooth initial data, with smooth extendibility beyond the $r=2m$ horizon characterizing Schwarzschild. This gives a strong asymptotic/rigidity result but the full uniqueness statement (and the Einstein–Maxwell analogue) as posed is generally regarded as partially solved rather than fully settled in all regularity classes.

status_evidence.title: Semi-global existence and convergence of solutions of the Robinson-Trautman equation
status_evidence.snippet: For smooth initial data, solutions of the Robinson-Trautman equation exist for all positive times and asymptotically converge to a constant curvature metric.
status_evidence.claim: Vacuum Robinson-Trautman solutions on S^2 x R converge to Schwarzschild.

status_evidence.title: On the Global Structure of Robinson-Trautman Space-Times
status_evidence.snippet: Evidence is given supporting the conjecture that no smooth extensions beyond the r=2m event horizon exist unless the metric is the Schwarzschild one.
status_evidence.claim: Smooth extendibility characterizes Schwarzschild among Robinson-Trautman solutions.
